reason: Jamku charges only ₹6,500 a year, so paying ₹12,990 upfront for a two-person practice that has run on Excel and WhatsApp for ten years feels unjustified. Unless software is dead simple and clearly proves its worth over our existing routine, I will not pay double when spreadsheets currently cost me nothing.
objection: Jamku charges only ₹6,500 a year—why is Docketra more expensive, and will it truly save me time during 10 PM ROC reviews instead of adding software overhead?
would_change_my_mind: Pricing matched to Jamku around ₹6,500 a year, or proof during busy season that the WhatsApp bridge and checklists genuinely save me hours of late-night ROC review with zero learning curve.
